cover: The cover of GPU Architecture & Parallel Programming from First Principles. Inside a glowing hive, the queen bee, wearing a crown and holding a sceptre, gives one order to the whole colony: c[i] = a[i] + b[i]. Below her, 32 worker bees in hard hats stand in 4 rows of 8, one warp, each in front of its own honeycomb cell and each filling it with honey at the same moment. One worker in the third row has wandered off on a branch of its own, with a question mark over its head. A crab in a hard hat waves from the corner, because the second half of the book writes kernels in Rust.
ch01: Tally, an ant, leads a column of ants carrying crumbs across a meadow. The column is wide where the ground is open, and every ant walks at once. Then it narrows to a single twig bridge over a stream, where only one ant can cross at a time and the rest wait in a queue. The bridge is the serial part of the work.
ch02: Comb, a worker bee in a hard hat, stands beside a hive with its side cut away. Inside hang three wooden comb frames, labelled SM 0, SM 1 and SM 2. On each frame small worker bees stand in straight rows that move together, a formation called a warp. Comb points at the frames like a guide on a tour.
ch03: The Queen bee, in her crown and sash, holds up a scroll that reads <<<4, 256>>>: a launch of 4 blocks of 256 threads. Beside her a wooden board holds 4 comb frames, labelled block 0 to block 3, and on each frame rows of worker bees wait for the order. The Queen gives one order and every bee on every frame carries it out.
ch04: Ferry, a pelican, stands on a wooden raft in the middle of a river, its beak pouch full of crates of bytes. On the left bank crates are stacked under a sign that reads host memory; on the right bank a sign reads device memory. A tag says pinned: 1 trip, because pinned data crosses in a single copy.
ch05: Whistle, a meerkat with a whistle, stands on watch beside a striped gate across a path. 3 worker bees have reached the gate and wait in a row; a 4th is still flying in from the left. The gate stays down until every bee has arrived. A sign on the gate reads __syncthreads(), and a tag says all arrive, then all go.
ch06: The otter twins float on their backs down 2 rivers that run side by side, each with a crate on its belly. Crates bob along both rivers at staggered places, so both streams carry work at the same time. Signs on the bank read stream 0 and stream 1, and a tag says 2 streams, at the same time.
ch07: Inch, a caterpillar, walks along a branch laid with numbered cells, 0 to 9 in order. Each of its segments stands over the next cell, so all of them step together and none reaches past its neighbour. A tag says neighbours read neighbours: the rule of coalesced memory access.
ch08: Stash, a red squirrel, sits on a tree stump beside a pyramid of acorns. The bottom row holds 8 acorns, the row above 4, then 2, then 1 at the top: each acorn stands for the 2 below it, so 8 values become 1 in 3 steps. Stash holds 1 more acorn in its paws. A tag says pairs, then pairs of pairs: the tree of a reduction.
ch09: Shell, a tortoise, walks across a meadow. Its domed shell is laid with square tiles in rows, like a matrix cut into blocks. Ahead of it lie 2 stacks of tiles, 1 marked A and 1 marked B, and behind it a finished row of tiles marked C. A tag says load a tile once, use it many times: the idea of a tiled matrix multiplication.
ch10: Hoot, an owl, sits on a tree stump at dusk and watches a rope of lanterns. The first 4 lanterns glow; a brace beneath them reads in scope. The last 2 hang dark; a brace beneath them reads scope ended. Nobody walked along the rope to put them out: each lantern switched itself off when its scope ended, as a C++ destructor releases what a constructor took.
ch11: Folio, an owl in reading glasses, stands in front of a tall bookcase. The shelves hold rows of books, and 6 of them face outwards with their titles: reduce, scan, sort, gemm, fft and rand, the ready-made kernels of the libraries. Folio holds 1 more book, marked BlockReduce, to lend to a kernel. A tag says tuned once, borrowed by every program.
ch12: Hue, a chameleon, grips a branch at dusk. On the left hangs a sheet of source code that the program has just written: float p, then lines of p = p * v plus a constant. Hue's body changes colour from tail to head, blue like the paper's ink at the tail, yellow at the head. Its tongue reaches out to a chip marked sm_87, the GPU the code is compiled for. A tag says written, compiled and loaded while the program runs.
ch13: Pinch, a crab in a hard hat, stands at a long table of numbered cells. Each claw picks up one input, a[i] in one and b[i] in the other, and the sum goes into the row c below. At the end of the row two small crabs have no cell to fill: they are the spare threads of the last block, and they doze.
ch14: Shuttle, a crab, walks along a long table of numbered cells, 0 to 15, coloured in a repeating pattern of 4. Dashed arcs mark its hops: from cell 1 to 5, to 9, to 13, always 4 cells at a time, and it fills every cell it lands on. 3 more crabs further back would cover the other colours. A tag reads i, i + stride, i + 2 stride: the grid-stride loop.
ch15: A pyramid of crabs on a sandy shore at dusk. 4 crabs on the sand hold up the products 2, 6, 3 and 4. On a rock above them, 2 crabs hold the sums of pairs, 8 and 7. On the highest rock, 1 crab holds the total, 15. A tag reads: pairs, then pairs of pairs.
ch16: Abacus, a crab, stands between a row of 4 cells and a column of 4 cells. 1 claw points along the row, 1 2 3 4, the other down the column, 1 0 2 1. Beside it stands a wooden abacus with 4 rods, and the beads pushed to the left on each rod are the 4 products, 1, 0, 6 and 4. A tag reads 1 + 0 + 6 + 4 = 11: 1 entry of C, computed by 1 thread.
ch17: Tiler, a hermit crab, walks along a beach under a shell built of square tiles. Behind it on the sand lie 2 tall stacks of tiles, marked A and B: the matrices in global memory. Ahead lies a small tide pool marked shared memory, where 2 tiles already rest, 1 from each stack. A tag says copy a tile once, read it 16 times: the idea of a tiled matrix multiplication.
ch18: Patch, a crab, stands on the sand beside a slate board. To the left of the board stand 2 cells of A, 1 and 5, and above it 2 cells of B, 1 and 0. On the board are their 4 products, 1 0 / 5 0. Further right, a larger board holds the 4 by 4 matrix C, 11 13 8 8 / 27 29 24 24 / 43 45 40 40 / 59 61 56 56, split into 4 coloured patches of 2 by 2, 1 per thread. A tag says read 4 values, make 4 products.
ch19: Ripple, a crab, stands on the sand beside a grid of square cells, 6 across and 6 down. The top row is hot, 100, and coloured red; the other edges are cold, 0, and blue. The inner cells shade from orange near the top to blue near the bottom, the final temperatures of a heated plate. 1 inner cell and its 4 neighbours are outlined in white. A tag says each cell becomes the mean of its 4 neighbours.
ch20: Rim, a hermit crab, carries on its back a square frame of 4 by 4 cells: the 4 inner cells are blue and the ring of 12 cells around them is amber, with the 4 corner cells grey. Behind it lies the sandy grid of a heated plate, with the same 4 by 4 square marked out where Rim lifted it. A tag says load the tile and its halo once.
ch21: Tally, a crab, stands on the sand in front of a row of 8 numbered pebbles, 3, 1, 7, 0, 4, 1, 6, 3. Under each pebble a running total is chalked on the sand: 3, 4, 11, 11, 15, 16, 22, 25. Tally holds a ninth pebble, the total 25, in one claw. A tag reads each total adds the one before it: a scan.
ch22: Bins, a crab, stands on the sand beside 4 crates labelled with the 2-bit digits 00, 01, 10 and 11. Chalked on each crate is the number of keys with that digit, 1, 2, 3 and 2, and above each crate the place where its first key goes, 0, 1, 3 and 6. Bins holds up a pebble marked 5, binary 101, on its way to crate 01. A tag reads count, scan, then place.
ch23: Lumen, a crab, stands on a beach at dusk beside a rope of 4 paper lanterns marked 1, 2, 3 and 4. Each lantern shines in proportion to the exponential of its number: the first glows faintly, and the last outshines the other 3 together. Tags under the lanterns give their shares of the light, 3%, 9%, 24% and 64%, which add up to 100%: the softmax of 1, 2, 3 and 4.
ch24: The whole crew of crabs stands on a beach at dusk in front of 4 framed pictures of the same scene, a house below a hill with the sun above. The first picture is in colour, the second in gray, the third blurred, and the last shows only white outlines on black. Arrows lead from each picture to the next, and a crab stands under each one, labelled grayscale, equalise, blur and sobel. A tag reads 4 stages, many images in flight.
ch25: Lens, a hawk, perches on a fence post at dusk with a stopwatch held up in one wing. Beside the post stands a board with 3 lanes of coloured bars, copies in, kernels and copies out, overlapping like the timeline of a profiler. A tag says measure, then change 1 thing.
ch26: Knock, a woodpecker, clings to a tree trunk and taps its beak on a brass doorbell plate fixed to the bark, marked with a register address. Beside the tree hangs a board with a ring of 8 slots: 5 of them hold work tickets, a PUT marker points past the last ticket written and a GET marker at the first ticket not yet done. A tag says write the work, then knock: the rule of a doorbell.
ch27: Weave, a spider, hangs at the centre of a web strung across a night sky. 8 green GPU chips, GPU 0 to GPU 7, sit at the ends of the spokes, and every spoke runs from a chip to the hub where Weave hangs. 4 silver knots on the spokes near the hub stand for the switches. With 1 thread from each chip to the hub, every GPU reaches every other through the hub, without a separate thread for each pair. A tag reads 1 link to the switch, not 7 to the others.
ch28: 4 geese stand in a ring on a meadow at dusk, each one a GPU of a ring all-reduce. A dashed path with arrows joins them in a circle. Each goose holds a parcel in its beak and faces the next goose, to which it hands its parcel. Around the ring from rank 0 the parcels read 1, 3, 6 and 10: a partial sum that grows as it travels. A tag says pass a chunk on, add your own, pass it on.
